overview: Saltasaurus loricatus was a relatively small (12-metre) titanosaur from the Late Cretaceous of northwestern Argentina (~70 Ma), remarkable for preserving direct evidence of titanosaur dermal armour: small bony nodules (osteoderms) embedded in the skin, including larger oval scutes up to 10 cm across. This was the first unambiguous evidence that sauropods could bear bony armour — previously considered impossible given their size and posture.

Saltasaurus is known from a nesting site (Auca Mahuevo) with hundreds of eggs preserved, some containing embryos and even embryonic skin impressions. This extraordinary site provides direct evidence of colonial nesting in titanosaurs, with many females laying eggs in the same area across multiple seasons.

fossilSites.name: Lecho Formation
fossilSites.note: Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian) continental deposits with Saltasaurus specimens including the armour-bearing material.

fossilSites.name: Anacleto Formation — Auca Mahuevo
fossilSites.note: Titanosaur nesting colony with hundreds of eggs, some with embryos and skin impressions; probably attributable to Saltasaurus or a close relative.

articles.title: Discovery and armour
articles.body: Described by Bonaparte and Powell in 1980 from Salta Province material. The bony osteoderms found associated with the skeleton were initially doubted as belonging to the same animal, but subsequent finds confirmed sauropod dermal armour. This armour may have provided defence against abelisaurid predators and possibly served a calcium storage function for egg production in females.

articles.title: Colonial nesting (Auca Mahuevo)
articles.body: The Auca Mahuevo site in Neuquén, excavated from 1997 by Chiappe, Dingus and colleagues, preserves a vast nesting colony of a titanosaur (almost certainly Saltasaurus or a close relative). Eggs are 13–15 cm in diameter; some preserve embryo skin showing small rounded scales. The site shows multiple nesting horizons — the same area used repeatedly across seasons — consistent with site fidelity in modern colonial nesters.

articles.title: Small size and late survival
articles.body: At 12 metres, Saltasaurus was small for a titanosaur. Its modest size and armour distinguish it from the giant titanosaurs of earlier Cretaceous South America. It survived until the very end of the Cretaceous, and its remains are found in Maastrichtian deposits just below the K-Pg boundary — one of the last non-avian dinosaurs known from South America.

fossilRecord.material: Partial skeletal material and skin/armour impressions.
fossilRecord.paleo: Late Cretaceous of northwestern Argentina, in floodplain environments with titanosaur nesting colonies.
fossilRecord.evidence: Bony armour plates embedded in skin are preserved — the first confirmed armoured sauropod — alongside typical titanosaur postcranial bones.

record.mya: late Campanian-early Maastrichtian, about 75-69 million years ago
record.description: Saltasaurus loricatus was a small-bodied saltasaurine titanosaur from the Lecho Formation of Argentina, known from disarticulated remains of several individuals and associated osteoderms.
facts: Much of the postcranial skeleton is known collectively, not as one complete individual.
Dermal armour is directly documented, but its complete arrangement over the body is unknown.

presentation.heroLead: A small, stocky titanosaur from Late Cretaceous Argentina and the first sauropod shown to carry bony armour in its skin, known from the mixed bones of several individuals.

heroMedia.title: Life restoration of Saltasaurus loricatus
heroMedia.alt: Life restoration of Saltasaurus, a short-necked sauropod with bony plates scattered along its back
heroMedia.caption: Life restoration by LadyofHats. The arrangement of the osteoderms, the skin texture and the colour are interpretive; the fossils give the plates but not their exact positions.

animalParagraphs: Saltasaurus was a titanosaur of modest size, probably between eight and twelve metres long depending on how the disarticulated bones are scaled. It had the wide-bodied, short-necked build typical of the most derived titanosaurs, with stout limbs and a broad, barrel-shaped trunk.

Its skin carried bone. Large oval plates up to about twelve centimetres across, together with many small ossicles, were found with the skeletons at El Brete, and their microstructure confirms they grew within the skin as dermal armour. How they were arranged over the body is not preserved, so restorations that show neat rows are guesses.

Like other titanosaurs it had a small head with narrow, peg-like teeth suited to cropping rather than chewing plants. Nearby fossil eggs and nesting sites in Patagonia are often linked to saltasaurines, but no egg has been tied directly to Saltasaurus itself.
animalHighlights: The first sauropod with directly documented dermal armour, changing how all titanosaurs were reconstructed.
A comparatively small, robust titanosaur with a short neck and wide stance.
Known from at least five individuals whose bones were mixed together at one site.

lifeCards.label: Feeding
lifeCards.level: Supported by teeth and jaw fragments
lifeCards.reason: Narrow, peg-like teeth and the sauropod body plan point to bulk cropping of vegetation. The specific plants eaten are not preserved.

lifeCards.label: Movement
lifeCards.level: Supported by limb and girdle bones
lifeCards.reason: Limb bones, the sacrum and pelvis show the wide-gauge, four-legged stance typical of derived titanosaurs.

lifeCards.label: Known size
lifeCards.reason: No single complete individual exists, so length and mass are scaled from bones of several animals of differing sizes.

lifeCards.label: Appearance
lifeCards.reason: Osteoderms are preserved and histologically verified as dermal bone, but their pattern on the body, and all colour, is reconstructed.

locality.name: El Brete
locality.note: A bonebed in the Lecho Formation that also yielded the enantiornithine birds first described from the site. The map shows a provincial reference rather than the exact quarry.

presentation.classificationSummary: Saltasaurus is the name-bearing genus of Saltasauridae and Saltasaurinae, a group of small, stocky, armoured titanosaurs from the latest Cretaceous of South America. Its close relationship with Neuquensaurus is well supported; broader titanosaur relationships remain unstable between analyses.

related.reason: A closely related, similarly small saltasaurine from Patagonia.
A Mongolian titanosaur often placed near Saltasauridae.
Compare with a giant titanosaur from the same continent.

questions.title: How was the armour arranged?
questions.copy: The plates and ossicles were found loose. Whether the large plates formed rows, a scattered mosaic or something else is not recorded by the fossils.

questions.title: Which bones belong together?
questions.copy: El Brete preserves several individuals mixed together, so the composite skeleton cannot be checked against a single articulated animal.

questions.title: Did it lay the Patagonian eggs?
questions.copy: Titanosaur nesting grounds in Argentina are often attributed to saltasaurines, but no embryo has been identified as Saltasaurus.

review.ageReviewNote: The Lecho Formation sample crosses late Campanian-early Maastrichtian estimates; a single 70 Ma date is too precise.

specimens.institution: Instituto Miguel Lillo, Universidad Nacional de Tucumán
specimens.note: Disarticulated bones of at least five individuals, including vertebrae, girdles, limb bones, teeth, braincase fragments and osteoderms.

panel.headline: Mixed bones of several individuals, plus the armour that made it famous.
panel.standfirst: Saltasaurus is known from a bonebed at El Brete that yielded disarticulated remains of at least five individuals, together with osteoderms. Collectively the sample covers most of the skeleton, but no single animal is complete.

coverage.label: Good
coverage.basis: Most postcranial regions and parts of the skull are represented across several individuals, but the bones are disarticulated and no complete or articulated skeleton is known.

knownRemains.title: What is actually preserved?
knownRemains.summary: Braincase fragments and teeth, cervical, dorsal, sacral and caudal vertebrae, ribs, the pelvis and shoulder girdle, forelimb and hindlimb bones, and numerous dermal plates and ossicles.
knownRemains.note: Because the material comes from several mixed individuals, reconstructions are composites and features such as the osteoderm arrangement cannot be read directly from the fossils.

materialGroups.label: Skull and jaws
materialGroups.value: Fragmentary braincase material and isolated teeth; no complete skull or lower jaw.

materialGroups.label: Vertebral column
materialGroups.value: Cervical, dorsal, sacral and caudal vertebrae from several individuals, including the holotype sacrum, with ribs.

materialGroups.label: Girdles and limbs
materialGroups.value: Ilia, ischia, pubes, scapulae and coracoids, with humeri, femora and other limb long bones.

materialGroups.label: Exceptional preservation
materialGroups.value: Dermal osteoderms and small ossicles, sampled histologically; no skin impressions, eggs or gut contents are attributed with certainty.

specimenCards.title: PVL 4017-92 · holotype
specimenCards.description: A sacrum fused to both ilia, chosen by Bonaparte and Powell in 1980 to anchor the species. It is one element of a large collection catalogued under PVL 4017 from the El Brete bonebed.
specimenCards.meta: El Brete, Salta · Lecho Formation · Instituto Miguel Lillo, Tucumán

specimenCards.title: PVL 4017 series
specimenCards.description: Disarticulated bones of at least five individuals of differing sizes, including vertebrae, girdles, limb bones and the dermal armour described in detail by Powell in 1992.

interpretation.label: Directly observed
interpretation.value: A holotype sacrum with ilia, mixed vertebral, girdle and limb bones from several individuals, teeth, braincase fragments and dermal osteoderms.

interpretation.label: Scientific interpretation
interpretation.value: A small, robust, wide-gauge titanosaur whose skin was reinforced with bony plates and ossicles, possibly as protection or as a mineral store.

interpretation.label: Still unknown
interpretation.value: The full skull, the arrangement of the armour, exact adult size, growth and which bones belong to which individual.
